newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher, techs steady.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher, techs steady.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to turn higher at the outset, aided by support for high tech and energy stocks after yesterday's drubbing.
A sell-off in shares of 3Com Corp, triggered by a profit warning for the current quarter, led the downward spiral in the techs Monday, but the sector stabilized in overnight trading in London.
"The techs got hit so badly yesterday that they will show some recovery today, as will the energy stocks," said Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities.

"Techs and energy issues outperformed the market and now they have run into some profit-taking and are dead in the water for the time being," she said. "But you usually don't see sectors get hit this badly for two consecutive days. There's nothing fundamentally wrong with the stocks, but it will take them time to rebuild their technical base and resume the uptrend."

Zagorski said that among energy stocks, oil services companies have had a strong run. She cited as an example Halliburton, saying it had risen from a low of 49-1/2 at end-September 1996 to 74 last month.
Both the bond market and the Standard & Poor's 500 March Index futures contract were higher ahead of the start of trading, indicating a steady opening.
The March futures contract rose 1.95 to 789.85.
"I think we will have a less volatile day," Zagorski said. "The techs are up in London and European markets behaved well, so I think that our market will straighten itself out today."
Shares of 3Com held fairly steady in after-hours trade Monday at 37-15/16. The stock lost 13-1/2 points during regular trading to close at 37-1/4.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average gained 314.13 points, or 1.76 percent, to close at 18,181.17.
U.S. technology shares firmed in London. IBM was up 1/2 at 143-1/4 while Intel Corp gained 7/8 to 152-1/2. Digital Equipment Corp rose 1/4 to 34-1/2.
Tobacco shares weakened amid worries about litigation. Philip Morris was down 3/8 at 119-7/8 and RJR Nabisco was 1/8 lower at 33-7/8.
The dollar was steady in sluggish Asian trade and probed above 1.67 marks in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were flat to slightly higher, with the long bond up 1/32 to yield 6.70 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's "Heard on the Street" column said Motorola Inc has had its troubles but hasn't changed its hardball tactics. By using its muscle recently to get payment of a $35 million bill, Motorola made sure it would emerge unscathed from the bankruptcy-court case of its big paging customer MobileMedia Corp.
The New York Times'a "Market Place" column said Yahoo! Inc and other Internet search companies have been building brand awareness through broadcast advertising.
